notes: Kingdom + regional identities + the duchies + the colonial territories. Iceland, Greenland and the Danish West Indies were all under the Danish crown throughout 1825–1875. The Schleswig-Holstein keys are deliberately ALSO members of tysk — the duchies were the contested ground of the 1848–51 and 1864 wars, and forcing them into one nation would take a side the register does not take.

Germany was not unified until 1871 — well inside the diary period — so the register names the individual polity far more often than "tysk". Kurland is included per its Baltic-German ruling class and German-speaking elite (it is also a member of russisk, having been annexed by Russia in 1795). Østrigsk is deliberately NOT a member: Austria was in the German Confederation until 1866 but is its own nation with its own substantial entry, and swallowing it would over-claim.

The register has no "Storbritannien" place entry, so this umbrella points at England. Ireland is included because it was part of the United Kingdom for the whole diary period (1801–1922) — a fact of the era, not a claim about Irish identity.
Frankisk is also a member of tysk — the Frankish realm straddled both later nations.
Italy unified in 1861, so pre-unification states (Naples, Genoa, Venice) dominate the register. Romersk here is Ancient Rome — geographically Italy; the register's own country label for it is "Rom".

Modern and ancient Greece in one place, as the classical entries (Attic/Athenian statesmen, Alexander) are the same cultural sphere the register treats them as. Østromersk (Byzantium) is Greek-speaking and also a member of tyrkisk, its territory becoming Ottoman. Makedonisk here is Ancient Macedon.
Maurisk (Moorish al-Andalus) is also a member of nordafrikansk.
The register uses "hollandsk" and "nederlandsk" interchangeably for the same country. Frisisk spans the Dutch, German and Danish North Sea coast and is a member of all three.
Flamsk is the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium.
Habsburg sphere. Bøhmisk is also a member of czekisk, tyrolsk also of italiensk (South Tyrol).
The modern demonym and the historical Bohemian one. No Czech place entry exists in the register — the country page will be absent, the persons will not.
Kurland was annexed by Russia in 1795; it is also a member of tysk for its German-speaking nobility.
Ottoman-era usage — the corpus predates the Turkish Republic. Armenians and Wallachia were both inside the Ottoman sphere in this period; valakisk is also a member of rumænsk.
Wallachia is one of the principalities that became Romania in 1859.
Finlandssvensk is also a member of finsk — that is precisely the identity it names.
A thin regional bundle for four otherwise-singleton keys. Deliberately not called "African" — it covers only the Mediterranean littoral the register actually touches.

Kept to the two genuinely supranational adjectives. The individual Nordic nations are NOT folded in: nobody in the register is described as "nordisk" merely by being Danish, and rolling them up would inflate this umbrella with people the source never labelled that way.
